recipes.name: Mom's Chicken and Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of celery soup

steps.text: In a large pot over high heat, combine chicken with enough water to cover; bring to a boil. Boil until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Drain some water, reserving 3 cups in the pot. Remove chicken, allow it to cool slightly, then pull it apart into bite-sized pieces and return to the pot.
Add condensed soup, season with salt and pepper, and set the heat to medium. Pull biscuit dough into pieces, and add it to the pot. Simmer until dough is cooked through, 7 to 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Chicken and Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: This old-time recipe for chicken and dumplings made with condensed cream of celery soup and refrigerated biscuit dough will bring back childhood memories.

review.reviewBody:
im only 13 and i could make this all by my self so it was really easy. i made some revisions to the recipe though such as, i changed the soup to creme of chicken and i also added another can of it to make 3. i also added a can of chicken broth instead of the 3 cups of water but then it was very chickeney so i added 1/2 a can of water. but for the briskets i added a lot more than lot called for and rolled them into balls before dropping them in. i dont know if you will like my changes but my parents said it was really good:)

-molly...if you like the revisions maybe you could add a review because i want to be a cook one day....thanks

GREAT basic recipe! I modified it a bit (like everyone else) as follows: Sauteed 1/8 c chopped onion and 1 lg. garlic clove (chopped) in 1 TBL butter before adding chicken. I used chicken tenderloin and covered it with 2 cans chicken broth. Did not drain any broth when chicken was done. Added 1 c cream of chicken, 1 c cream of mushroom and 1 can cream of celery soup and 1/2 box frozen peas and carrots. I used two cans of Pillsbury buttermilk biscuits and after sprinkling about 1 TBL of Wondra (very fine) flour on a paper plate, cut them into a tic-tac-toe pattern. I dusted the dumplings with the flour on the plate and put 1/2 of them in the pot to cook (when it was boiling). They took about 15 minutes. After we had eaten all of the dumplings in the pot, I turned the heat back on, let it come to a boil again and cooked the remaining dumplings for the leftovers. Without the dumplings crowding into each other, they plumped nicely, didn't stick together and there were plenty for the leftovers.

Turned out great. I did edit like other comments mentioned. Used half low sodium Chicken broth and then I added one can of chicken soup instead of two cans of celery soup. I also cut up carrots and celery and boiled it in the water with some garlic and onions before hand. I boil the chicken and then I removed it and then for the dumplings and then add it all together at the end after the dumplings were done.

I don't even like chicken and dumplings, and this was fantastic. I made it like this: 1 can veggie broth, 1 can of chicken broth w/ three chicken breasts (I don't like dark meat). I used one can of cream of celery, and one of cream of chicken. I also added about a cup of frozen peas and carrots. I used JP's Big Daddy Biscuits recipe from this site for the dough and used about half of it (I made biscuits out of the other half). I cooked it about 5 minutes longer than called for once the biscuits were in because I didn't feel they were cooked enough at 8 minutes. A fabulous, quick and filling meal. I brought it to my husband's work for him and a co-worker, and the co-worker said it was the best home-cooked meal he'd had in a long while. *ear to ear grin*

Thank you for the recipe base! I had never made chicken and dumplings before your recipe showed up on my email and I thought I'd give it a try. I read through about 50 comments and took a lot of those into making my own recipe I want to give you five stars for your basic super easy recipe I never imagined using biscuit dough for the dumplings but it turned out great! I used pillsbury grands biscuits and cut each with a ticTac toe pattern as one reviewer suggested I sautéed my chicken thighs in olive oil garlic, onions and S& P cut the chicken into chunks and poured the juices in the pot I did not use water, i used 2 C organic chicken broth, 1 can each of cream of celery soup and cream of chicken soup 1 white onion, Baby carrots and 2 stalks of celery, salt and pepper to taste

A good home made chicken stock is essential to producing great results ! I use a whole chicken. I use enough water to cover the chicken and then add the following. 2 bay leaves, 1 whole onion chopped, 3 stalks of celery and a couple/few chopped carrots. Fresh herbs are best but store bought will do. I use Italian seasoning (approx 3 tsp.), Rosemary, thyme, and smashed garlic. Some salt and pepper to taste. When the chicken is finished cooking then strain the stock well to remove any small bones, remove the bay leaves, and return it to the pot. I use 1 can of cream of chicken soup with herbs. Whisked in well with the stock and then add about a 1/2 cup of whole milk or 1/2 & 1/2 (what ever you have is fine)....Bring the whole thing up to a gentle boil, and start dropping in the torn or cut biscuits. I quarter mine and then add them slowly. Put the lid on it and let the dumplings cook (they puff up) while watching carefully not to burn the pot. Adjust the herbs/seasoning to taste. I realize I've made a lot of changes here but the extra time to make your own stock will make all the difference in the world. Wishes to you all for happy cooking.

I used leftover chicken from a roasted chicken and I added vegetables from the refrigerator that I wanted to use up (carrots, corn, peas and green beans). I used "Roasted Chicken Better than Boullioun" in my water to give it a nice chicken flavor, a can of cream of mushroom soup and a can of cream of celery. I also sautéed onions, celery and garlic in butter when I started the base. I had some heavy cream in the refrigerator so I poured some of that in too for a creamy soup. I didn't have canned biscuits, but I had a box of the Red Lobster Cheesy Biscuit mix, so I whipped that up and used that for the dough. My family loved it, and my husband said the Cheesy Biscuits was the secret ingredient that made it so much more flavorful including the cheddar cheese. This is an awesome base recipe that you can just add whatever to and it's delicious. It was a great way to use up some leftovers and I already had the canned soups in my pantry. Yay!

This was sooo easy and delicious! I made a couple changes...I used chicken breast tenderloins and cooked them in two cans of Swanson's chicken broth. I added diced potato to the broth. Separately I sauteed diced onion in some butter and then added a tablespoon of minced garlic. Then added this to the broth with the chicken. I also added baby carrots and minced celery and a bay leaf. Later I added 1 can of cream of chicken and 1 can cream of celery soup and poured in 1/4 cup of heavy cream...I simmered until the potato and carrots were tender..added sea salt and freshly ground pepper, tossed in some frozen peas, and topped with the biscuit dough. Cooked as the recipe said and served. My guest loved it and so did I! Total comfort food!!

I was very hesitant to make this, but with all the great reviews, I decided to give it a try. I made many changes based on the reviews -- used breast meat in place of thighs and bumped the number of cans of soup up to 3, with one of them being cream of chicken soup. I also added diced onion, celery and carrot to the mix plus salt and pepper to taste (I probably had a little more than three cups of broth in my pan). I was very surprised at how good this was with those changes. That being said, it wasn't much easier than my regular chicken and dumpling recipe, but my husband loved the soup, while I loved how easy and mess-free it was to make the dumplings. Next time I'll probably try a hybrid with this soup recipe and my own dumplings. All in all, very tasty.

I agree that this recipe is a good base recipe. I boiled my chicken in a pot filled over half full f water. Seasoned water with garlic powder onion powder basil thyme pepper and a little salt. I saved all the water, After cutting up chicken I added it back to the remaining water and then added the biscuit dough let it come back to a boil turned down to low and added 2 cans of mixed veggies and let simmer for 15 mins. I did not add the creamed soup because the biscuit dough thickens the stock nicely.

Simple and delicious! The only adjustments I made to the recipe were cooking the chicken in chicken broth instead of water along with a blend of chopped onions, celery, and bell peppers. After adding the chicken back to the broth, I added a mixture of chopped carrots, green beans, and corn. It turned out so yummy!

You can add whatever you like to this recipe and it is delicious. I used chicken broth instead of water. Added salt, pepper, garlic, onion and a can of peas. I used butter flavor biscuits and it was so good!

Great base for modifying any way you like. I used what I had in chicken, 3 thighs, and 6 legs. Also added a can of biscuits. I also used the natural broth without adding any more. This made 6 healthy delicious bowls. *I made this in an Instant Pot as well.
Used chicken broth instead of water, added frozen carrots & peas. A few cloves of garlic & diced onion
I loved it and added a can of corn, pea's, and carrots and even that much better
I added peas and potatoes

It is a very good starting point recipe. Play around with the ingredients by adding different spices, herbs, veggies, etc.! Make it your own version. I saw a tip recently to freeze your dumplings before adding them to the pot to prevent them from sticking to each other. I'm trying that today. I'm using Pillsbury pop biscuits. No need to criticize this recipe! Just make it your own!
Good recipe. Added diced potato and carrots and onion.
The picture looked good, too bad the finished product as written was not good

I added 1 small white onion. Minced garlic. Also veggies (celery, corn, carrots, string beans and peas). I used sally, pepper, seasoned salt, salt free garlic and herb seasoning. Also a dash of crack seasoning. Also 2 table spoons of butter and flour to thicken. Super good!!
